A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same survey, with readable main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and Appendix A. Content can be matched despite reordered sections and repagination.

before.justification: V1 synthesizes results attributed to cited studies. Its figures are schematics, its tables organize literature, and Appendix A catalogs resources; no original experimental or data-analysis results are reported.

after.justification: V2 remains a literature survey. The added methodological discussions, reported findings, and benchmark descriptions concern other researchers' work, without original experiments or analyses in the main text or appendix.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes a predictive algorithm whose procedure changes. Algorithm 1 remains unchanged; newly covered architectures are additions to the surveyed literature, not modifications to a method proposed by this work.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts training or evaluation on datasets. The additional weather-model examples and Appendix A benchmarks expand literature and resource coverage, without adding tasks actually evaluated by the survey.

E2.justification: No evaluated comparator set is added or revised. Newly discussed methods are literature examples rather than baselines tested against a proposed approach.

E3.justification: No experimental protocol, split, metric, or training budget is introduced or revised for this work. Added descriptions of published models do not establish changes to existing evaluations.

E4.justification: V2 adds discussion of robustness-oriented methods and physical constraints, but no new ablation, sensitivity test, error analysis, or supplementary experiment. These additions remain summaries of related research.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its own results. Expanded uncertainty-quantification discussion in Section 6 concerns modeling literature, not statistical reporting practices.

E6.justification: V2 adds qualitative findings attributed to cited studies: adaptive PINN sampling reduces errors without increased computational cost (Section 3.3), and auxiliary PINN losses can hinder neural operators (Section 3.4). Existing quantitative comparisons are retained. These are newly summarized findings, not original experimental results.

T1.justification: V2 adds mathematical qualifications, including convexity and a strict Hamiltonian minimum for stable Port-Hamiltonian models (Section 3.2), and the infinite-penalty limit connecting soft and hard conservation constraints (Section 4.3). Existing numbered formulations are substantially retained, with no new proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a broad survey organized around knowledge-driven and data-driven physics priors, supplemented by industrial applications and an open-source overview. The revised positioning and conclusion do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds caveats about ill-conditioned Lagrangian Hessians, neural-operator boundary compliance, and deployment costs. It clarifies observed-trajectory intersections for augmented ODEs and revises Table 1's applicability classifications, including changing neural operators from system inference to simulation solving.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the existing software catalog and PDEBench entry while adding descriptions and access links for PDEArena, APEBench, nn-benchmark, and The Well. These improve resource documentation without documenting new experiments.

R1.justification: The literature coverage expands substantially across constrained and spectral operators, stable Port-Hamiltonian networks, MetaPhysica, DINo/CROM, CoDA, and newer weather models including Prithvi-WxC, GenCast, and PreDiff. The introduction also explicitly distinguishes the survey from Wang and Yu (2021). These exceed bibliographic maintenance.

P1.justification: The algebraic-structure and PINN-loss sections exchange positions, several headings change, and selected background passages, transitions, and concluding paragraphs are rewritten. Front matter and acknowledgments are updated, while the overall organization and most existing exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 receives a categorical legend and expanded caption, and Table 1 gains more descriptive headers. Figures 2 and 3 exchange numbering and placement; Table 3 is relocated. All eight schematics are retained, alongside added journal headers and ordinary text reflow.

improvement.justification: V2 fills useful coverage gaps in constrained operators and probabilistic weather forecasting, adds applicability cautions, and expands the benchmark resource guide. These improve the survey's usefulness without transforming its central synthesis. Redundant Figure 1 caption prose and an incomplete sentence in Section 3.5 temper the editorial gains.
